correctness.rationale: For all m>=1, the geometric-sum/Binet calculation yields exact integer identity 7*window=g*f_g(B_{n+m}). Modulo 7, both B and g have explicit three-cycles, giving 7|f_g(B_s); direct arithmetic at B1=1 and B2=6 shows gcd(f_g(1),f_g(6))=7 (2,3,5 excluded; v7(f1)=1; all p>=11 excluded by 3A-32H=21). Invertibility of the balancing recurrence state mod d makes B1,B2 recur in every tail, forcing the polynomial tail gcd to be exactly 7. Cancelling gives exact g for every n and m. The supplied 910 finite identities and 70 two-value gcd tests only corroborate the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact odd-window all-shifts gcd is a natural number-theoretic invariant already studied for first powers of balancing numbers. Establishing its unexpected exact stability for cubes in every odd window length, explaining the irreducible factor seven through an integer polynomial and universal modular period, meaningfully advances that program. It cannot be extrapolated to arbitrary odd powers: seventh powers at length three have gcd 49 versus 7. Unlike a routine isolated experiment, this is an infinite exact classification with a structural proof.
